column3: NASB renders “be destroyed” as “is torn down” and reorders the verse.
NASB adds “house” and reorders the verse.
NASB reads “having put it on,” following other manuscripts; the critical text has “having put it off.”
NASB follows the critical text (“because”); it adds “while.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “for this very thing” as “for this very purpose” and “the pledge of the Spirit” as “the Spirit as a pledge.”
NASB renders “being confident” as “being always of good courage” and ends the verse with a dash.
Close to the Greek.
NASB adds “I say” and renders “confident” as “of good courage” and “are pleased” as “prefer.”
NASB renders “we are ambitious” as “we have as our ambition.”
NASB follows the critical text (“bad”); “be revealed” is rendered “appear,” and “receive back” is “be recompensed for.”
NASB restructures the verse.
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “an answer” and renders “occasion of boasting” as “an occasion to be proud.”
NASB renders “we are crazy” as “we are beside ourselves.”
NASB follows the critical text without “if”; “compels” is rendered “controls.”
NASB adds “on their behalf.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “know” as “recognize” and “regarded” as “known.”
NASB follows the critical text (“new things”); “creation” is rendered “creature.”
NASB follows the critical text without “Jesus.”
NASB renders “how” as “namely,” “reckoning” as “counting,” and “put into us” as “committed to us.”
NASB renders “beseeching” as “entreating” and “implore” as “beg you.”
NASB follows the critical text without “For.”
